If all the cells have been filled, then the puzzle is solved. Otherwise, the algorithm tries each possible combination for the next cell until it finds one that satisfies the rules of Sudoku. If no solution is found, the algorithm backtracks to the previous step and tries another combination. This process continues until the puzzle is solved. The algorithm also uses heuristics such as checking if there is only one valid option left for a particular cell before trying other combinations. This helps reduce the search space and speeds up the algorithm. Finally, the algorithm checks if the current configuration of the board violates any of the rules of Sudoku after every move.
